extracted.intended_audience: prospective authors and peer reviewers for PeerJ (researchers submitting manuscripts to PeerJ)
extracted.subtask_description: Journal-level editorial criteria used by PeerJ editors and reviewers to evaluate submitted manuscripts across Research Articles, Literature Reviews, Method Papers, and Data Reports. Focuses on basic reporting, experimental design, and validity of findings for each article type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review philosophy: rigorous yet fair; judge soundness not importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Rigorous yet fair review. Judge the soundness of the science, not its importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions are not made based on any subjective determination of impact, degree of advance, novelty or being of interest to only a niche audience. PeerJ will also consider studies with null findings. Replication studies will be considered provided the rationale and how it adds value is clearly described. Studies that are redundant or derivative of existing work will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Article — Basic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission must adhere to all PeerJ policies. The article must be written in English, use clear, unambiguous, technically correct text, and conform to professional standards of courtesy and expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poorly written manuscripts will be returned to the author. Include sufficient introduction and background to demonstrate how the work fits into the broader field and appropriately reference relevant prior literature. Structure should conform to an acceptable format of 'standard sections' (see Instructions for Authors); significant departures only if they improve clarity or conform to discipline-specific custom. Figures should be relevant, of sufficient resolution, appropriately described and labeled. The submission should be self-contained, represent an appropriate unit of publication, include all results relevant to the hypothesis, and coherent bodies of work should not be inappropriately subdivided merely to increase publication count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Article — Experimental design
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission must describe original primary research within the Aims & Scope of the journal and clearly define the research question and knowledge gap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The investigation must have been conducted rigorously and to a high technical standard. Methods should be described with sufficient information to be reproducible by another investigator. The research must conform with prevailing ethical standards in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Article — Validity of the findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Data should be robust, statistically sound, and controlled; data underlying conclusions must be provided or made available in an acceptable discipline-specific repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclusions should be appropriately stated, connected to the original question, and limited to those supported by the results. Claims of causation must be supported by well-controlled experimental intervention (correlation is not causation). PeerJ considers null findings and replication studies if justified. Redundant or derivative studies will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature Review — Basic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The review should be of broad and cross-disciplinary interest and within the scope of the journal; the Introduction must adequately introduce the subject, audience, and motivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the field has been reviewed recently, authors must justify the new review (different point of view, accessible to a different audience, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature Review — Experimental design (survey methodology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey methodology must be consistent with comprehensive, unbiased coverage of the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If coverage is not comprehensive/unbiased, reviewers should identify what's missing. Sources must be adequately cited (quoted or paraphrased as appropriate). The review should be organized logically into coherent paragraphs/subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature Review — Validity of the findings
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be a well-developed and supported argument that meets the goals set out in the Introduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Conclusion should identify unresolved questions, gaps, and future directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method Paper — Basic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Must describe a new or significantly improved method/protocol, or the adaptation or reuse of an existing method in a new domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple descriptions of a protocol are not considered sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method Paper — Experimental design
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must articulate the need for the method and be accompanied by any data used to develop and validate the method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any materials required to complete the method must be available and described with enough detail to allow others to obtain them. The method should be compared to existing methods, ideally by direct comparison using the same materials, or otherwise by citing appropriate literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method Paper — Validity of the findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Advantages and disadvantages of the method compared to available alternatives must be described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible advantages/disadvantages should be quantified. Improvements may include reduced cost, improved accessibility, greater specificity/sensitivity, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Report — Basic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes new curated dataset(s) or major extensions of an existing dataset of interest and value to the research community; rationale and utility beyond a single research paper must be clearly articulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should, where possible, follow the form of a research article with methodology described to allow replication/reproduction. Materials/specimens should be deposited in an appropriate public repository where relevant. The dataset must either be uploaded with submission or linked to a publicly accessible repository with a DOI and be available under a free and open license. Data must be in a usable and accessible format and accompanied by sufficient metadata to allow reuse (following FAIR principles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Report — Experimental design
rubrics_metrics.description: If the dataset is expected to be extended over time, authors must provide details of ongoing curation, inclusion/exclusion criteria, storage, and availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PeerJ's usual requirements for ethical approval, consent, field permits, and so on apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Report — Validity of the findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptive statistics may be included with Data Reports, but submissions that analyze the dataset to test hypotheses and reach conclusions should be submitted as Research Articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data Reports are intended primarily to document and make available datasets rather than to present hypothesis-driven analyses.
